transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-03
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Avery Collins (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Maya Lin (Redwood SE), Laura Jenkins (Northstar Head of ML), Mark Rivera (CTO), Sameer Khan (Infra Lead), Priya Desai (Security)

Summary: quick discovery call to understand Northstar's workload, sizing, security needs, and procurement timeline.

[00:00] Avery Collins: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intros, I'm Avery on the Redwood sales team, Samir and Maya from our solutions engineering side. Laura, Mark, do you want to kick off?
[00:18] Laura Jenkins: Yeah thanks, uh hi all. I'm Laura, Head of ML at Northstar. We're evaluating options for serving a set of LLMs in production — low latency for customer-facing features, and some internal batch scoring. Mostly looking at dedicated GPU pools for predictability and data isolation.
[00:35] Mark Rivera: Hi, CTO here. Key things for us: latency SLOs, predictable unit economics, and we need the infra to sit in our GCP VPC with strict egress rules.
[00:50] Samir Patel: Got it. When you say latency SLOs, what numbers are you targeting (p50/p95)?
[00:58] Laura Jenkins: p50 around 80-120ms for the small models, p95 ideally < 400ms; for large models we can accept higher but we want consistency.
[01:12] Sameer Khan: Also, we'll need dedicated isolation — can't have other tenants on the same GPUs. So reserved capacity, ideally single-tenant.
[01:25] Maya Lin: That makes sense. Redwood Dedicated supports reserved pools with single-tenant tenancy. We also do prefix caching and KV cache to help latency for repeated requests — helpful for chat histories.
[01:40] Priya Desai: Security: we require SOC2, ISO27001, SSO (SAML/Okta), KMS integration, and audit log retention for 1 year. Also curious about customer-managed keys vs Redwood-managed.
[01:56] Avery Collins: We have SOC2 and ISO docs; we'll send the security pack after this call. For KMS we support both Redwood-managed and customer-managed (bring-your-own keys) with HSM integrations for Private deployments, and for Dedicated we can integrate with your KMS in the VPC.
[02:15] Laura Jenkins: Great. On capacity: roughly how many GPUs would we need? Our traffic right now is ~120 qps peak across 3 models, with spikes to 250 for a few minutes during batch runs.
[02:30] Samir Patel: Ok rough calc: model size + throughput matter — are these 7B, 13B, 70B families? Also average sequence length and top-k sampling vs deterministic generation affects tokens/sec.
[02:44] Laura Jenkins: Mostly 13B and 70B variants, the 70B is used for longer form summarization internally, 13B for customer-facing completions. Sequence length avg ~256 tokens, sometimes 1024 for summaries.
[02:58] Samir Patel: Understood. For that mix, we'd propose a base reserved pool sized for steady qps — maybe a mixture of A100/80GB or equivalent. Then configure a burst pool for short spikes. Redwood Dedicated supports burst capacity (shared across customers in your account) and auto-burst rules into a secured, limited pool.
[03:18] Mark Rivera: Is burst still single-tenant? We can't have noisy neighbors from other customers using our burst pool.
[03:26] Maya Lin: Yes, burst in Dedicated is scoped to the customer's account. It's not cross-tenant. The difference is whether it's pre-reserved or on-demand — we offer a small committed burst buffer and the option to expand at higher unit cost if the policy allows.
[03:41] Sameer Khan: How fast is autoscale? We have short 5-10 minute spikes during release windows; need capacity to ramp without queuing.
[03:50] Samir Patel: Our autoscale targets node spin-up within 2-5 minutes depending on instance type and region — we also recommend warm standby nodes for very tight windows. With reserved Dedicated capacity you can set minimum node counts to avoid cold starts.
[04:06] Laura Jenkins: Cool. On cost — we need pricing for reserved committed capacity vs on-demand. CFO will want comparisons.
[04:15] Avery Collins: We'll send a pricing sheet with monthly and annual commit tiers, expected unit token cost assumptions, and examples based on your qps profile. Typically commits give ~20-35% discount vs pay-as-you-go.
[04:30] Priya Desai: About data residency: all inference must occur within our GCP VPC in us-central1. Can Dedicated run in a customer VPC?
[04:39] Maya Lin: Yes — Dedicated supports customer VPC deployments with private networking. For fully on-prem or air-gapped, that would go into our Private product, but for VPC we can deploy Dedicated nodes that sit in your network and use customer KMS.
[04:54] Mark Rivera: If we go VPC, what does control plane look like? We still want Redwood to manage runtime but not have access to raw inputs.
[05:03] Samir Patel: We offer a hybrid: control plane in Redwood with audit logs shipped to your SIEM, and optional data plane that stays in your VPC. We can redact payloads and disable telemetry if needed — all configurable via policy.
[05:20] Sameer Khan: Can you run benchmarks for us? We'll want a pilot where we run our prompt sets and measure latency and throughput and token costs.
[05:28] Avery Collins: Absolutely. Typical pilot is 2-3 weeks. Samir will coordinate the bench harness and we can run it in a dedicated pilot pool sized to your expected load.
[05:38] Laura Jenkins: That works. Also interested in model variants and quantization. We may want int8 quant for cost reasons on some workload.
[05:47] Samir Patel: We can support multiple quantization profiles; for 13B models int8 often gives 2-3x throughput improvements with small quality delta; 70B quantization is trickier but we have verified 4-bit/8-bit options for certain families. We'll include recommended quantization profiles for your models.
[06:03] Mark Rivera: Any SLA on latency and uptime for Dedicated? Our app is customer facing.
[06:10] Maya Lin: Dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime and latency targets tied to reserved capacity tiers. Exact numbers depend on commit level and region; we'll include SLA details in the contract docs.
[06:22] Priya Desai: One more security question — audit logs retention, can we set retention to 12 months and export to our logging?
[06:29] Samir Patel: Yes — audit logs can be exported to your logging bucket or SIEM and retention configured. We'll include instructions for log forwarding.
[06:38] Laura Jenkins: On timeline — we want to pilot in the next 2-3 weeks and be ready to decide by end of August. Procurement is slightly slow but if the pilot looks good we'll aim for a Q4 commit.
[06:50] Avery Collins: Sounds good. We'll aim to have pricing and security pack to you by Wednesday. Samir will send the pilot plan.
[07:00] Mark Rivera: Ok, one last thing — switching cost. If we later need Private (air-gapped), what does migration look like?
[07:08] Maya Lin: We design the deployment to be portable — same API surface, model pinning, rollouts. Private requires more provisioning and longer lead times, but we can migrate model artifacts and configs. We'll document the migration plan as part of the engagement.
[07:23] Laura Jenkins: Thanks. That covers most of it.
[07:27] Avery Collins: Great. Next steps recap: send security docs and pricing, Samir to share pilot plan and bench scripts, schedule follow-up for 2026-08-17.
[07:38] Laura Jenkins: Thanks everyone.
[07:40] (call ends)

Notes about transcript: occasional transcription errors present, some acronyms mis-cased (KV cache vs K V), some speaker overlap where lines may be attributed incorrectly.
